prompt: Complete ObjectUtils with a null-safe equality helper sameContent and a classNameOf method that reports an object's simple class name, returning "null" for a null reference.
explanation: Calling a.equals(b) directly would throw a NullPointerException when a is null, so the helper first handles the null cases with reference checks: a == b covers both-null (and same-object), and one remaining null means the values differ. Every object inherits getClass() from java.lang.Object; it returns the RUNTIME type, and getSimpleName() strips the package, turning java.lang.Integer into "Integer". This is essentially how java.util.Objects.equals is implemented.
hints: Start sameContent with reference checks: if a == b you can return true immediately (this covers two nulls).
After that, if either argument is null the other cannot equal it -- only then is it safe to call a.equals(b).
For classNameOf, guard against null first, then use o.getClass().getSimpleName() -- getClass() reports the object's actual runtime class.
